newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil lower, meal mixed on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil lower, meal mixed on USDA report.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures were lower at midsession while soymeal prices were mixed as the market reacted to conflicting messages from USDA's Supply/Demand Report, traders said.
USDA on Tuesday pegged U.S. soybean output at 2.403 billion bushels, above average trade expectations. But the report also showed an increase in Chinese demand for soymeal.
China was expected to buy 1.6 million tonnes of soymeal, up from last month's projection of 1.4 million tonnes.
USDA also increased its soybean crushing rate figure to 1.390 billion bushels, up from 1.375 billion last month.
Traders noted cash basis values in the country remained strong and crush margins were high. Soybean crushing rates were near record highs in October yet demand outpaced supply.
"That meal spread is going to stay strong until crush is able to keep up with demand," a trader said, noting a $9.30 premium December over the January.
At 1150 CST, soyoil futures were 0.25 to 0.11 cent per lb lower with December down 0.16 at 22.59. Soymeal was up $1.00 to down $1.50 per ton with December up $1.00 at $227.70 a ton.
